name: Tessera Chronos Field Disruptor CFD-1 'Lag Spike'
description:
A classified experimental weapon that projects a localized temporal distortion field — an area approximately 3 meters in diameter where the passage of time is slowed relative to the surrounding environment. Targets within the field experience subjective time normally, but external observers see them moving at approximately one-tenth normal speed.

Tessera's quantum physics division developed the Chronos Disruptor based on theoretical work suggesting that gravitational manipulation at extreme intensities can produce time dilation effects. The CFD-1 does not stop time — it creates a steep temporal gradient that slows all processes within the field, from chemical reactions to neural signaling to projectile trajectories.

The weapon is Tessera's most classified project, with fewer than five operational units in existence. The temporal distortion field persists for approximately 10 seconds before the quantum effects collapse, and the energy required to maintain even this brief distortion requires a power system that occupies a small vehicle. The man-portable designation is generous — the weapon is backpack-mounted and requires a two-person crew.
specifications: caliber: N/A — projected temporal distortion field effective_range: 10-40 meters (field projection point) rate_of_fire: 1 field per 120 seconds (quantum field regeneration) capacity: 3 fields per power cell weight: 38 kg (weapon and power system, two-person crew) power_source: Experimental quantum power cell, non-rechargeable
tactical_use: The Lag Spike is deployed to freeze high-value targets in relative time, allowing operators to approach, restrain, and extract them while they are effectively immobilized. From the target's perspective, they see the world suddenly accelerate — operators appear to move at ten times normal speed, and they are restrained before they can react. The weapon has also been used to freeze incoming projectiles in flight, creating a brief window where a protected area is effectively immune to ballistic threats.
cultural_context: The CFD-1's existence is unknown to the general population of GLMZ. Among the handful of individuals who have encountered its effects, the experience is described as profoundly disorienting — the world seems to jump forward, with gaps in memory and perception that feel like a corrupted recording. Tessera's quantum physics division treats the project with religious secrecy, and personnel involved in its development are forbidden from acknowledging its existence even within Tessera's own corporate structure.
story_hooks: A security camera in a Tier 4 corridor recorded footage that appears to show time moving at different speeds in different parts of the frame — people on the left side of the image moving normally while people on the right appear frozen. The footage has been classified and the camera's storage has been seized.

A CFD-1 field collapsed prematurely during a classified operation, and the temporal gradient's sudden equalization produced a burst of exotic radiation. Three operators are experiencing time at a slightly different rate than the surrounding world — they are aging faster than normal, and Tessera cannot fix it.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, angular backpack-mounted device resembling a hybrid between advanced medical equipment and experimental physics apparatus. Dominates the wearer's silhouette with a pronounced upper framework featuring a forward-projecting emitter assembly. The overall aesthetic suggests cutting-edge corporate R&D rather than traditional weaponry — more laboratory than battlefield.
physical_description.dimensions: Backpack frame: 65cm H × 48cm W × 28cm D. Emitter pod extends 35cm forward from shoulder mounting. Power system occupies 22cm × 19cm × 16cm integrated into lower frame.
physical_description.weight_description: Substantial and balanced — 38kg distributed across dual shoulder mounts and lumbar support straps. The weight is high but engineered for stability during sustained wear. Requires training to operate efficiently; feels unwieldy to the untrained.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade carbon composite frame with titanium alloy joint reinforcements. Emitter pod constructed from brushed chromium-vanadium steel with embedded quantum field coils visible through transparent polymer viewport.
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal composite body with brushed metallic accents. The emitter pod features polished chrome paneling with micro-etched quantum circuit patterns. Power cell housing in gunmetal grey with faint iridescent shimmer from active quantum suspension.
physical_description.color_scheme: Dominant charcoal grey with titanium silver accents. The emitter pod glows faint blue during standby due to internal quantum field stabilization. Accents of dark cyan along power distribution conduits.
physical_description.grip_texture: Dual ergonomic control grips wrapped in high-grip rubberized polymer with embedded haptic feedback nodes. Shoulder straps utilize memory-foam padding with military-spec anti-slip webbing. Secondary hand-cranked stabilizer grips feature bare titanium with knurled surfaces.
distinctive_features: Transparent quantum viewport revealing impossible geometric field patterns shifting within the emitter pod
Array of seven blue and amber status LEDs along the right shoulder mount — temporal field coherence indicators
Hairline fractures in the viewport crystal suggesting previous field collapses or containment stress
Faint burn marks around the emitter aperture — evidence of temporal gradient plasma discharge
Humming resonance from active quantum field stabilizers — barely audible 40Hz vibration
Nested Faraday cage mesh visible under composite paneling, indicating extreme EM shielding requirements
Hand-scrawled maintenance notes in Cyrillic script on lower power cell housing — jury-rigged field repairs
Quantum entanglement calibration ports sealed with military-grade tamper indicators
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Embossed 'TESSERA CHRONOS FIELD DISRUPTOR CFD-1' designation on upper frame in sans-serif font. Empathic Analytics corporate logo (nested Φ symbol) appears on shoulder straps in holographic foil — visible only at certain angles. Serial number etched into titanium joint: heavily redacted with industrial-grade scratch-out. Warning labels in three languages stamped on power cell housing, partially obscured by field service modifications.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained but clearly field-tested. The weapon shows signs of intense use within classified operations — carefully preserved core systems, but evidence of emergency repairs and field modifications. Hairline fractures in viewports suggest multiple temporal field collapses. Scuff marks and impact dents consistent with rapid insertion/extraction operations. The device maintains operational integrity but appears exhausted by its experimental nature.
